claims.statement: EU law defines an aggregation contract that customers may enter without their electricity supplier's consent, and permits consented dedicated-meter data for settlement of flexibility services; this creates a contractible route to dispatch rights over heat pumps, batteries and EV chargers, although Polish implementation and market access still need verification.

Polish dynamic tariffs expose eligible customers to 15-minute wholesale-linked price variation, while URE says shifting consumption is intended to reduce emergency renewable shutdowns; only 4,836 households used dynamic contracts by end-2025, so the loss is real price volatility and unmonetised flexible load, but adoption remains very early.

The immediate payer is a heat-pump, battery or EV-owning household or microenterprise, with the electricity bill as budget and tariff sign-up or a large bill swing as trigger; URE found dynamic offers already carry wholesale markups of PLN 0.0999-0.149 per kWh and monthly fees up to PLN 49.90, showing an existing paid retail-service layer.

contrary_evidence: URE reported only 4,836 Polish household dynamic-tariff customers at end-2025 despite much broader smart-meter availability, so customer willingness may be weak.
Suppliers may exclude negative wholesale prices, add caps or fees, and Polish rules may not yet make independent small-load aggregation economically accessible.

economics.acquisition_route: Use the founder's parents' renewable installer as the first channel: add an opt-in aggregation and device-control agreement to heat-pump, battery and EV-charger installations, then recruit other regional installers under revenue share.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Validate with 50 controllable homes, reach 2,000 devices and roughly PLN 1.2m annual recurring revenue, then expand through installer channels to 20,000 devices; at PLN 6m-9m recurring revenue and positive margins, retained founder equity plus accumulated cash could plausibly exceed PLN 5m in 5-7 years without assuming a sale.
economics.founder_time: Part-time founder builds forecasting, dispatch and settlement logic for 3-4 hours daily; certified electrical work and customer support are handled by installer partners, with a market-access specialist contracted before any live aggregation.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Software orchestration and settlement should be high margin after device/API and market-access fees; preliminary target is 55-70% gross margin, unproven until a Polish balance-responsible partner quotes terms.
economics.payback: Charge no hardware subsidy initially; customer payback is targeted below 12 months from verified bill savings, while acquisition spend should recover within 6-9 subscription months.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: PLN 39-79 per connected premise per month plus 15-25% of verified flexibility or bill savings; alternatively wholesale the fleet to an energy retailer for a per-device availability fee.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Monthly service persists while the controlled asset and tariff remain active; accumulated device response curves, comfort constraints and settlement history improve dispatch and retailer bargaining power.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A proprietary response-and-comfort dataset across heterogeneous devices improves dispatch accuracy, while a larger fleet earns better market-access terms and attracts more installers.
fingerprint.customer: Polish households and microenterprises with heat pumps, batteries or EV chargers, initially installed by regional renewable-energy contractors.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Installer-embedded opt-in at equipment sale and service visits, followed by energy-retailer white-label distribution.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Automated flexible-load dispatch sold as a subscription plus savings share, with optional wholesale capacity payments from a licensed market-access partner.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The asset owner pays when dynamic-tariff volatility or inflexible consumption raises the bill; later a retailer or aggregator partner pays for dependable pooled flexibility.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Installation of a controllable electric asset, adoption of a dynamic tariff, or an unexpectedly high electricity bill.

founder_fit: The parents' renewable-energy installation company supplies an unusually direct pilot channel and trusted field-service capacity.
Forecasting, optimisation and device telemetry use the founder's data-science strengths and can be developed part-time.
The model is system-led and partner-distributed rather than dependent on a personal brand or continuous founder selling.
risks: Polish licensing, balancing responsibility, telemetry and minimum-bid requirements could make direct market participation unobtainable for a small entrant.
Device manufacturers can restrict APIs, and bad dispatch could damage equipment, comfort or trust.
Retail price protections or supplier formulas can eliminate the savings pool.

structure.control_point: Consent-backed dispatch and settlement rights over installed flexible electrical loads
structure.critical_dependency: A lawful Polish market-access and balance-settlement partner with usable device telemetry

thesis: Acquire contractual dispatch rights at the moment a regional installer commissions a heat pump, battery or charger, pool those assets, and sell owners automated bill optimisation before monetising the same fleet as verified flexibility through a market-access partner.
title: Installer-Locked Flexible Load Fleet
uncertainties: Exact Polish independent-aggregator registration, minimum bid size and settlement economics are not yet verified.
Actual savings after distribution charges, taxes, comfort limits and supplier markups are unknown.
It is unknown whether installer customers will grant durable remote-control rights.
